name: United States (federal)
note: Deaths are registered by the States, not the federal government. The federal layer receives deaths mostly through voluntary State contracts with SSA (42 U.S.C. 405(r)), now largely by Electronic Death Registration, plus funeral-director SSA-721 forms and family reports. SSA then passes death data to CMS, VA, other benefit payers and Treasury's Do Not Pay, but by law keeps State-furnished deaths out of the Death Master File that NTIS sells. Private-sector checks (the Limited Access DMF) therefore see only part of the picture. The IRS and passports depend on the family.

steps.title: State vital records office sends death records to SSA (EDR and State Death Match)
steps.localName: Electronic Death Registration (EDR) / State Death Match
steps.who: Each State vital records office (bureau of vital statistics) under a voluntary contract with the Commissioner of Social Security.
steps.trigger: Official filing of a death certificate with the State.
steps.summary: Under 42 U.S.C. 405(r) States voluntarily contract to furnish SSA with information on deaths whose certificates have been filed, and SSA pays a fee and the transmission cost. With Electronic Death Registration (EDR), the State verifies the SSN with SSA first and then sends the death report, on which SSA terminates benefits without further verification. States participate by contract, not by federal mandate.

steps.title: Funeral director reports the death to SSA (Form SSA-721)
steps.who: The funeral director handling the remains.
steps.summary: SSA adds death data from Form SSA-721, Statement of Death by Funeral Director, to the Numident, and it counts as preferred proof of death. No federal statute found makes this report compulsory; it is SSA procedure. Where the form names a surviving spouse or children, SSA sends a survivor-benefits letter.

steps.title: Family or representative payee reports the death to SSA
steps.who: First-party reporters: a relative (spouse, parent, sibling), the representative payee or an agent; third parties such as a friend may also report.
steps.summary: SSA takes death reports from many sources. First-party reports from acceptable reporters are not verified. Third-party reports for beneficiaries must be verified before benefits stop. These reports go to the Numident through the Death Information Processing System (DIPS), which passes them to the payment systems automatically.

steps.title: CMS, VA, OPM and State agencies report deaths to SSA
steps.who: CMS, the Department of Veterans Affairs, OPM and State agencies other than vital records.
steps.trigger: Learning of a beneficiary's death in their own programmes.
steps.summary: Death reports from other agencies arrive as third-party alerts. SSA must verify them before posting the death to the Numident for a beneficiary.

steps.title: SSA death data reaches Medicare (CMS)
steps.who: SSA and HHS/CMS under a data-matching agreement.
steps.summary: Section 405(r)(10) requires SSA to agree to data matching with HHS when HHS or its Inspector General asks. Medicare Part A entitlement ends on the day of death. Discrepancies between SSA's and the Medicare (HI) record of the date of death raise alerts that SSA resolves.

steps.title: SSA shares State death data with other agencies paying federally funded benefits (e.g. VA)
steps.who: Federal or State agencies paying federally funded benefits, such as the Department of Veterans Affairs, under cooperative arrangements with SSA.
steps.summary: SSA must, to the extent feasible, give death information to other agencies paying federally funded benefits through reimbursable cooperative arrangements. Those agencies may use it only for that purpose. VA benefits stop from the last day of the month before death.

steps.title: SSA's full death file (including State data) feeds Treasury's Do Not Pay
steps.who: SSA, giving data to the Treasury Bureau of the Fiscal Service, which runs the Do Not Pay working system.
steps.summary: Every executive agency must check SSA's death records through Do Not Pay before paying. From 27 December 2023, 405(r)(11) gave Do Not Pay State-reported death data for a 3-year period. Pub. L. 119-77 (2026) replaces this, from 27 December 2026, with continuing access and bars SSA from recording a death without clear and convincing evidence. States and their contractors also have access to Do Not Pay.

steps.title: State vital records send death data to NCHS (National Vital Statistics System)
steps.who: State and registration-area vital records offices, paid by NCHS for the federal share of costs.
steps.summary: NCHS collects data each year from State and municipal death records that meet its standards, and pays the federal share of the cost of collecting and transcribing them. This is a cooperative arrangement, not a federal mandate on the State.

steps.title: Consular officer records a U.S. citizen's death abroad (CRODA)
steps.who: A U.S. consular officer (Department of State).
steps.trigger: Local death certificate or local finding of death abroad.
steps.summary: When a U.S. citizen dies abroad, the consular officer prepares a Consular Report of Death Abroad. It is based on the local death certificate and filed with the Vital Records Section of Passport Services. Certified copies go to the next of kin.

steps.title: Copies of the consular report go to agencies paying the deceased
steps.who: Department of State, sending copies to each agency concerned.
steps.trigger: A CRODA for a federal payee, federal employee or Selective Service registrant.
steps.summary: If the person who died abroad received continuing federal payments, was a federal employee or was a Selective Service registrant, the original report goes to the Department with one copy for each agency concerned.

steps.title: Executor tells the IRS by filing the final return and notice of fiduciary relationship
steps.who: The executor, administrator or other person in charge of the decedent's property.
steps.trigger: The death; the filing deadline for the year of death.
steps.summary: Nothing found sends the death automatically to the IRS. The final income tax return must be filed by the executor or administrator. A fiduciary gives notice to the IRS (Form 56), and a refund is claimed with Form 1310.

steps.title: NTIS sells the Death Master File; the most recent 3 years only to certified subscribers (LADMF)
steps.who: SSA supplies the DMF to the Department of Commerce (NTIS), which sells it. Recent deaths go only to persons certified under 15 CFR part 1110.
steps.trigger: A death recorded by SSA from a non-State source.
steps.summary: Deaths in the last three calendar years are released only to certified persons with a legitimate fraud-prevention interest, or a legitimate business purpose under law, regulation or fiduciary duty. The DMF excludes deaths SSA received from States under 405(r), so the public file is missing much of the death data. SSA sends corrections when a living person is wrongly listed.

steps.title: Treasury reclaims post-death benefit payments from the bank
steps.who: The Treasury Bureau of the Fiscal Service on behalf of the paying agency, by notice of reclamation to the receiving bank (RDFI).
steps.trigger: The agency learning of a recipient's death after payments were credited.

deadline.text: agency must request reclamation within 120 calendar days of first knowledge of the death

steps.summary: When a federal benefit recipient has died, the paying agency may reclaim post-death payments from the receiving bank. That notice is often how the bank learns of the death. The bank must return benefit payments received after it becomes aware of the death. The reclamation request must be made within 120 days of the agency's knowledge.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No federal population register. SSA's Numident (SSN records with death data) is the closest thing, but other bodies get its death data only by statute-specific arrangements: 405(r) cooperative arrangements, Do Not Pay, and the DMF/LADMF.

governmentPropagation.note: For federal benefit payers, mostly automatic: State EDR feeds reach SSA (where the State has a contract), and SSA passes deaths to CMS, VA and other benefit agencies and to Do Not Pay. Not automatic for the IRS, which the executor tells by filing; and no domestic passport-cancellation feed was found.

privateSectorVerification.note: Through NTIS, the Limited Access DMF is available to certified private users; the Open Access DMF is public after 3 years. The DMF excludes all State-furnished (405(r)) deaths, so private checks miss a large share of deaths. No law requires banks, insurers or credit bureaus to check it. The FCRA imposes no death-reporting duty on credit bureaus.

gaps: ssa.gov and www.ssa.gov answer 403 to this session (origin refusal), so SSA's public DMF, EDR and 'what to do when someone dies' pages could not be read. Only POMS on secure.ssa.gov was reachable.

No federal statute found makes funeral directors file Form SSA-721; the duty, if any, comes from State law or SSA's request. The POMS page on SSA-721 completion (expected under GN 02602.060) returns 404.

The Treasury Do Not Pay site (fiscal.treasury.gov), NTIS/LADMF (ntis.gov, ladmf.ntis.gov), CMS, VA, travel.state.gov, govinfo.gov, congress.gov and law.cornell.edu were blocked at the egress proxy, so agency guidance on DNP death-data use, LADMF fees and Medicare death processing was not read.

OLRC's note under 42 U.S.C. 405 calls the 2026 Do Not Pay amendment Pub. L. 119-76 in one place and Pub. L. 119-77 in another (140 Stat. 745). The Statutes at Large text was not checked (govinfo blocked).

No federal law or regulation found tells the IRS of a death automatically, or makes the State Department cancel a deceased citizen's passport domestically. Both rest on the family (or on SSA data-sharing agreements not found in public law).

FCRA (15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.) was searched for any duty on credit bureaus to flag a death. None was found (15 U.S.C. 1681c contains no death provision), so credit bureaus learn of deaths from the LADMF or the family.
Whether every State has an active 405(r) contract and EDR, and how quickly deaths are transmitted, is not set by federal law and was not established.
